title.narrative: Provision of integrated lifesaving nutrition services to drought affected population living in the rurals of Jowhar district of Middle Shabelle region.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="background-color: white color: black font-family: Helvetica, sans-serif"gtARD will intervene with a nutrition project with the objective to contribute to reduction of mortality and morbidity among 13,500 beneficiaries Children U5 (10600 boys and 12200 girls) and 4800 PLWs that result from acute malnutrition by treating uncomplicated SAM and integrating with basic nutrition service package (BNSP) linked to WASH and health programs in the drought affected settlements among Jowhar rural in the towns of Mahaday and Jilyale district and 35 nutrition staff and 32 CNWs trained. The Outcome of the project will be to increase access to emergency nutrition services to children under five and pregnant and lactating women in drought affected populations living in the rurals of Jowhar district. The activities will include: Screening and treatment of 4800 (2800 pregnant women and 2000 lactating women) and 7000 (3200 boys and 3800 girls) with acute malnutrition Provision of prevention and management of common childhood illnesses (Malaria, Diarrhoea and Pneumonia) Training of 35(15 male and 20 female) Nutrition staff in Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition, EPI/NHHP and GBV/PSEA and AAP Training 32(12 male and 20 female) Community Nutrition Workers on basic Infant Young Child Feeding (IYCF-E) Provision of multiple micro nutrients to 4000 pregnant women and 3000 lactating women Provision of 9500 children (4500 boys and 5000 girls) 6-59 months with Multiple Micro Nutrient Supplementation Provide Individual counselling and/or breastfeeding support for 2500 mothers of SAM children admitted to the program Provision of Vitamin A supplements to 9500 children under five (4500 boys and 5000 girls) 6-59 months Providing 9500 children (4500 boys and 5000 girls) 6-59 months with deworming tablets at the nutrition sites Provide maternal and child health and nutrition promotion messages using billboards and other IEC materials.
